# Best Attendance & Payroll Software for Logistics & Transport Companies in India (2026)


October 19, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/best-attendance-payroll-software-for-logistics-transport-companies-in-india-2026/#respond)


**Short answer:** For small to mid-sized logistics firms, fleet operators, and courier companies in India (10–500 employees), **SalaryBox** (from ₹27/employee/month) delivers the best combination of GPS-based field attendance, live location tracking, and automated payroll with PF/ESI compliance. For large logistics enterprises with 1,000+ workers across multiple depots, **Keka** or **Darwinbox** offer deeper multi-entity payroll and workforce analytics. If you’re a startup with under 25 staff, **greytHR** ‘s free plan gets you off spreadsheets at zero cost.


India’s logistics sector employs over **22 million people** ([LSSC](https://www.logisticsinsider.in/indias-logistics-sector-to-need-47-lakh-additional-workers-by-2030-lssc-ceo/) ) and is growing at a **10.7% CAGR** ([Mordor Intelligence](https://www.mordorintelligence.com/industry-reports/india-logistics-market) ), with a projected need for **4.7 million additional workers by 2030** ([Logistics Insider, citing LSSC](https://www.logisticsinsider.in/indias-logistics-sector-to-need-47-lakh-additional-workers-by-2030-lssc-ceo/) ). Yet most transport operators still process payroll manually, spending **3–4 days every month** matching check-in records with dispatch logs before salaries go out. Meanwhile, India faces a severe driver shortage: for every **100 trucks, there are only about 55 drivers** , down from 75 a few years ago, leaving roughly **20 lakh (2 million) trucks idle** ([DAT Freight Analytics](https://dat.com/blog/trucking-is-the-backbone-of-indias-economy) ).


When you’re already short-staffed, losing drivers over payroll disputes is a problem you can solve with software. We evaluated **16 HR and attendance platforms** to find the 10 that work best for Indian logistics, transport, courier, and fleet companies in 2026.

## How Did We Evaluate Attendance Software for Logistics Companies?


We tested 16 platforms against five criteria weighted specifically for the logistics and transport industry’s unique operational needs:


1. **GPS and field attendance (25% weight):** Transport workers don’t sit at a desk. Drivers start from different pickup points daily, delivery riders cover varied routes, and warehouse staff rotate across depots. The software must support GPS-verified check-in from any location, not just a fixed biometric terminal.
2. **Route and KM tracking (20%):** Fuel reimbursements, per-trip incentives, and overtime disputes all depend on accurate route data. Platforms that track daily kilometres and route history score highest here, this is what separates logistics-ready software from generic HR tools.
3. **Mixed pay structure handling (20%):** A typical transport company has salaried drivers (₹20,000–25,000/month), daily-wage warehouse helpers (₹350–450/day), and per-consignment delivery riders all on the same payroll. The software must handle multiple pay types in one cycle.
4. **Statutory compliance (20%):** About **80% of the transport workforce** earns under the **₹21,000/month ESIC ceiling** , making ESI registration mandatory. PF, Professional Tax, and TDS add layers. Overtime must be calculated at **twice the ordinary wage rate** per the Factories Act.
5. **Multi-depot management and cost (15%):** Logistics companies operate from multiple warehouses, depots, and city hubs. The software needs centralized dashboards with location-specific attendance zones. Affordable pricing matters because driver margins are thin.


## What Are the Best Attendance & Payroll Platforms for Indian Logistics Companies in 2026?


### 1. SalaryBox — Best Overall for Small to Mid-Sized Logistics & Fleet Operations


**Quick take:** SalaryBox combines GPS and selfie-based field attendance with live location tracking and fully automated payroll ,built for workforces that operate from the road, not from a desk. At ₹27/employee/month with no minimum headcount, it’s priced for the thin margins transport companies operate on.


**Why it works for logistics:** SalaryBox’s core strength for transport companies is its GPS attendance with live location tracking. Drivers and delivery staff check in via selfie plus GPS from wherever their day starts, a warehouse, a client site, or a pickup point. Managers see a real-time map of who’s checked in and where. The route history feature logs daily kilometres and locations visited, which directly feeds into fuel reimbursement verification and per-trip incentive calculations. The payroll engine handles PF, ESI, TDS, and Professional Tax automatically, including separate pay structures for salaried drivers, daily-wage helpers, and contract loaders. Geo-fenced attendance zones let you set up virtual boundaries around each depot so warehouse staff can only mark attendance when physically present.


**Pricing:** ₹27 per employee per month. Free trial available. No minimum employee requirement.


**Limitations:** Best suited for operations up to 500 employees. Doesn’t offer AI-powered demand forecasting for seasonal headcount planning. No on-premise option, cloud-only. Advanced fleet management features (vehicle tracking, fuel management) require separate fleet software.


**Ratings:** 4.7/5 on Google Play Store (12,500+ ratings) · 4.7/5 features on Capterra

The geo-fenced hub attendance on paid plans lets you set warehouse and depot zones so staff mark attendance only from verified locations. greytHR has **15+ years of experience** with Indian payroll compliance, which means edge cases like mid-month joiners, full-and-final settlements for departing drivers, and multi-state Professional Tax are well-handled. The employee self-service portal lets drivers view payslips and apply for leave from their phones.

**Limitations:** No route or KM tracking — you can verify someone checked in at the depot, but not where they went during the day. This makes fuel reimbursement and per-trip incentive verification manual. Seasonal headcount spikes increase costs on per-employee pricing. The free plan has limited reporting and no geo-fencing. ### 3. Keka — Best for Mid-to-Large Logistics with Multi-Entity Payroll


**Quick take:** Keka’s strength for logistics is its multi-entity payroll engine and advanced pay structure configuration. If you run a transport business with 200+ employees across multiple states, each with different PF rates, Professional Tax slabs, and overtime rules, Keka handles the complexity without manual intervention.


**Why it works for logistics:** Keka supports multiple pay groups within a single payroll cycle, which means salaried fleet managers, daily-wage loaders, and per-consignment delivery riders all process through one system with their own rules. Its expense management module handles fuel receipts, toll reimbursements, and travel claims, the expenses that pile up in transport operations. The overtime module calculates at the legally required **2x ordinary wage rate** and feeds directly into payroll. Shift scheduling supports rotational patterns for warehouse operations. Keka’s attrition analytics flag flight-risk employees, critical in an industry where competitor poaching is common, with dispatch staff being offered **₹500–1,000 more** to switch.


**Pricing:** From ₹6,999/month + ₹60 per employee. No free plan.


**Limitations:** Too expensive for fleets under 50 employees. No built-in route or KM tracking — fuel reimbursement verification requires manual uploads or integration with fleet management tools. Setup takes 1–2 weeks. The interface has a learning curve for non-technical transport managers.


**Ratings:** 4.5/5 on G2 (1,400+ reviews) · 4.5/5 on Capterra

### 4. Zimyo — Best for Courier & Delivery Fleets with Trip-Based Pay


**Quick take:** Zimyo stands out for courier and last-mile delivery companies because of its field force module with trip-based check-ins and per-trip incentive configuration. If your delivery riders are paid per consignment or per route, Zimyo builds that directly into the payroll cycle.


**Why it works for logistics:** Zimyo’s field force module lets delivery staff check in at the start of each trip, log delivery stops, and check out at completion, creating a trip-by-trip attendance trail. Per-trip and per-consignment incentives can be configured as payroll components that auto-calculate based on completed trips. The platform covers PF, ESI, Professional Tax, and TDS, and supports **30–100 employee teams** , the sweet spot for city-level courier operations. GPS-verified attendance ensures riders are at their assigned pickup points. The self-service app lets riders track their trip counts and projected incentive earnings in real time.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing (per head/month). Free demo available.


**Limitations:** No free plan. Heavier than what a 10-person micro-fleet needs. No biometric hardware bundling, warehouse attendance requires separate biometric device integration. KM-based tracking is less detailed than dedicated fleet management tools. Limited multi-entity payroll for companies operating across many states.


**Ratings:** 4.5/5 on G2 (500+ reviews)


### 5. FactoHR — Best for Multi-Depot Transport with Complex Compliance Needs


**Quick take:** FactoHR’s combination of AI-powered contactless attendance, custom compliance rules, and multi-entity support makes it a strong choice for established transport companies operating across multiple depots and states. If your primary pain point is configuring Motor Transport Workers Act rules alongside standard PF, ESI, and Professional Tax across multiple states, FactoHR handles that compliance depth.


**Why it works for logistics:** FactoHR’s contactless AI face recognition works without touching a shared device — practical for warehouse environments where gloved or dirty hands make fingerprint scanners unreliable. The platform supports custom compliance rules, which means you can configure the **Motor Transport Workers Act, 1961** requirements (rest intervals, maximum driving hours, welfare provisions) alongside standard PF/ESI/TDS. Multi-entity payroll handles different state-level Professional Tax slabs and overtime rules per depot. Contract staff management with expiry alerts tracks driver license renewals and vehicle permits. It holds ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certifications for data security.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing (quote required). Free demo available.


**Limitations:** No transparent pricing — you must request a quote, which is a friction point for small operators. No built-in route or KM tracking. The platform is feature-dense and can feel overwhelming for single-depot operations. Implementation may take 2–4 weeks for complex setups.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 (400+ reviews)


### 6. HROne — Best for Multi-City Transport Chains


**Quick take:** HROne serves **2,000+ Indian companies** and is built for operations that span multiple cities. For a transport company with depots in Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, and Hyderabad — each running different shift patterns and state-specific payroll rules — HROne’s centralized dashboard with location-level policy flexibility is the key differentiator.


**Why it works for logistics:** HROne’s multi-branch architecture lets each depot set its own attendance rules, shift timings, and leave policies while headquarters maintains a consolidated payroll view. Geo-fenced attendance zones ensure depot staff check in from the correct location. The multi-state payroll engine automatically applies the correct Professional Tax slabs, ESI contribution rates, and overtime rules for each branch’s state. The mobile app lets branch managers approve leaves and view attendance without logging into the desktop portal — useful for depot supervisors who spend most of their day on the warehouse floor.


**Pricing:** Custom pricing based on employee count and modules selected.


**Limitations:** Not ideal for operations under 50 employees, the platform is built for scale. No route or KM tracking for field staff. No transparent pricing. Mobile app reviews are mixed. Limited customisation for non-technical users who need to configure transport-specific pay rules.


**Ratings:** 4.6/5 on G2 (800+ reviews)

With **80 lakh+ registered SMEs** on the platform and a free tier, it’s built for owner-operators who track salaries on paper notebooks today.


**Why it works for logistics:** PagarBook’s selfie-plus-location check-in is simple enough for non-tech-savvy drivers to use. The advance tracking feature lets you log fuel advances, toll money, and on-route cash disbursements then deduct them automatically from the month-end salary. This solves a persistent pain point for small transport operators: reconciling the ₹500 cash advances given every other day to drivers for fuel and food. Basic salary calculation, advance deduction, and payment tracking are free. Paid tiers add features like SMS payslips and staff categories.

**Limitations:** No route or KM tracking. Statutory compliance support is basic, PF and ESI calculations work, but complex multi-state scenarios may need manual handling. No multi-branch consolidation for growing fleets. No shift scheduling or rotation management. Not suitable once you cross ~25 employees, the platform is designed for micro-operations. No desktop interface; mobile-only.

## Which Attendance & Payroll Software Should Your Logistics Company Choose?


The right platform depends on your fleet size, the types of workers you employ, and how many locations you manage:


**For micro-fleets and single-truck operators (5–25 employees):** Start with **PagarBook** (free) if you just need basic salary tracking and advance management, or **greytHR** (free up to 25) if you want proper statutory compliance with PF/ESI/TDS automation.


**For small to mid-sized fleets and courier companies (25–500 employees):** **SalaryBox** (₹27/employee/month) is the strongest choice — it’s the only affordable platform combining GPS field attendance, live route tracking, and automated payroll. Drivers check in from the road, managers track locations in real time, and payroll runs with full compliance.


**For courier and delivery firms with per-trip pay structures:** **Zimyo** offers the best trip-based check-in and per-consignment incentive configuration, built specifically for delivery fleet operations.


**For multi-depot transport companies (200–1,000 employees):** **Keka** for multi-entity payroll with advanced expense management, or **HROne** for the best centralized multi-branch dashboard with location-specific policies.


**For enterprise logistics and 3PL groups (1,000+ employees):** **Darwinbox** for AI-driven workforce planning and enterprise-grade analytics, or **Keka** if you need faster implementation at a lower price point.


**For compliance-heavy, multi-state operations:** **FactoHR** for the deepest custom compliance rule configuration, including Motor Transport Workers Act requirements.


## Why Do Indian Logistics Companies Need Dedicated Attendance & Payroll Software?


India’s logistics sector is the backbone of its economy, handling nearly **70% of domestic freight** and moving over **4.6 billion tonnes of goods annually** across a road network spanning **6 million+ kilometres** ([DAT Freight Analytics](https://dat.com/blog/trucking-is-the-backbone-of-indias-economy) ). The **$140 billion road freight industry** supports roughly **12.5 million trucks** , projected to reach 14–15 million by 2028. And the sector is adding jobs fast — TeamLease projects **10 million new logistics jobs by 2027** ([Maritime Gateway](https://www.maritimegateway.com/logistics-sector-likely-to-add-10-million-jobs-by-2027-teamlease-services/) ).


But the workforce reality is harsh. India has just **55 drivers for every 100 trucks** , down from 75 a few years ago — a ratio that has left **2 million trucks sitting idle** . Average driver salaries sit at **₹20,000–25,000/month** , while warehouse helpers earn **₹350–450/day** . In Tier-1 cities, dispatch staff are regularly poached for just **₹500–1,000 more per month** . More than **50% of truck drivers develop health problems** by their early 40s, with **60–70% reporting back and cervical pain** by age 42 ([Kantar IMRB study via DAT](https://dat.com/blog/trucking-is-the-backbone-of-indias-economy) ).


In this environment, payroll errors and attendance disputes aren’t just operational headaches — they directly cause driver attrition that you can’t afford when there’s already a 45% driver gap. The average company makes **15 errors per payroll cycle** , each costing **₹24,000+ to fix** , and **24% of employees start looking for a new job after just one payroll error** ([G2, 2025 via Petpooja](https://blog.petpooja.com/people-payroll/payroll-hr-technology-statistics-india/) ). For a transport company losing a driver over an ₹800 overtime dispute, automated payroll isn’t a luxury — it’s retention infrastructure.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Which is the best attendance and payroll software for logistics companies in India?


For small to mid-sized logistics firms and fleet operators (10–500 staff), **SalaryBox** offers the best combination of GPS-based field attendance, route tracking, and automated payroll at ₹27 per employee per month. For large logistics enterprises with 1,000+ employees across multiple depots, **Keka** or **Darwinbox** provide deeper multi-entity payroll and workforce analytics. Budget-conscious startups can begin with **greytHR** ‘s free plan for up to 25 employees.


### How do logistics companies track attendance for drivers and field delivery staff?


Logistics companies use GPS-based mobile attendance apps that let drivers and delivery staff check in from any location using selfie verification plus GPS coordinates. The software logs the check-in location and time, creating a verifiable attendance trail without requiring a fixed biometric terminal. Some platforms like **SalaryBox** and **Zimyo** also track live routes and daily kilometres, which helps reconcile fuel reimbursements and per-trip incentives.


### What payroll challenges are unique to transport and logistics companies in India?


Transport companies face several unique payroll challenges: mixed pay structures (daily-wage loaders, salaried drivers, per-consignment incentives), route-based overtime that varies by trip distance, fuel and toll reimbursements that must be reconciled with attendance data, seasonal headcount spikes during festival and e-commerce sale periods, and the fact that roughly **80% of the transport workforce** falls under the **₹21,000/month ESIC ceiling** requiring mandatory ESI contributions. Most transport operators spend **3–4 days each month** manually matching check-in records with dispatch logs before processing salaries.


### Is GPS attendance tracking legal for transport employees in India?


Yes, GPS-based attendance tracking is legal in India when employees are informed and give consent. Under the **Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP) 2023** , employers must clearly communicate that location data is being collected, the purpose of collection, and how it will be stored. Most attendance apps include consent prompts during onboarding. The key legal requirement is transparency, covert tracking without employee knowledge can attract penalties under the DPDP Act.


### How much does attendance and payroll software cost for a logistics company in India?


Attendance and payroll software for Indian logistics companies typically costs between **₹40 and ₹200 per employee per month** . **greytHR** offers a free plan for up to 25 employees. **SalaryBox** starts at ₹80/employee/month with GPS tracking included. **Keka** starts at ₹6,999/month plus ₹60 per employee. Enterprise platforms like **Darwinbox** offer custom pricing for large fleets. Budget options like **PagarBook** offer free basic tiers for micro-operations.


### Can payroll software handle per-trip and per-consignment incentives for drivers?


Yes. **Keka** and **Zimyo** allow trip-based or per-consignment incentive rules to be configured alongside base salary. **SalaryBox** supports custom pay components that can be adjusted monthly. For complex incentive structures (distance-based slabs, volume-based bonuses), platforms like **FactoHR** and **Darwinbox** offer formula-based pay component builders where you define the calculation logic once and the system applies it automatically each payroll cycle.


### What compliance rules apply to payroll for transport workers in India?


Transport companies must comply with: **EPF** (Employees’ Provident Fund) for establishments with 20+ employees, **ESI** (Employees’ State Insurance) for workers earning up to ₹21,000/month covering roughly 80% of transport workers, **Professional Tax** that varies by state, **TDS** (Tax Deducted at Source), and overtime calculated at **twice the ordinary wage rate** under the Factories Act and Shops & Establishments Act. The **Motor Transport Workers Act, 1961** adds sector-specific rules on working hours, rest intervals, and welfare measures for drivers.


### How do I manage attendance across multiple depots and warehouses?


Multi-depot logistics operations need software with **geo-fenced attendance zones** , each depot or warehouse is set as a location, and staff can only check in when GPS shows they are within that zone’s radius. Platforms like **SalaryBox, HROne** , and **greytHR** support multiple geo-fence locations under one account with a centralized dashboard. **Keka** and **Darwinbox** go further with multi-entity payroll, allowing each depot to follow state-specific compliance rules while headquarters consolidates reports.
